summary:

title: EU's goods exports to Canada reach $54.8 bn in 2025
summary:
European Union goods exports to Canada reached €48.8 billion (~$54.8 billion) in 2025, while imports were €33.0 billion (~$37.1 billion), leaving a €15.8 billion (~$17.8 billion) surplus.
Exports rose 1.2 per cent from 2024 and imports increased 18.0 per cent.
Machinery led EU exports; ores, slag and ash were the top import group, the Eurostat data showed.

title: Vietnam-Cambodia trade grows as countries pursue $20 bn target
summary:
Vietnam-Cambodia bilateral trade rose 8.3 per cent year on year to $8.7 billion in the first eight months of 2026, as both countries pursue a $20 billion target. 
Growth is supported by complementary industries, Vietnamese investment in Cambodia and improved border infrastructure, with better transport links expected to reduce logistics costs and strengthen cross-border supply chains.

title: Netherlands' goods exports rise 4.9% in August
summary:
Netherlands' goods export volume rose 4.9 per cent year on year in August 2026 on a working-day-adjusted basis, after 2.3 per cent growth in July, according to the CBS.
Machinery shipments increased in particular and transport equipment was also higher; goods imports rose 2.0 per cent, led by machinery and electronic products, while October export conditions were more favourable than in August.

title: Bangladesh releases $40.6 bn export incentives for FY27
summary:
Bangladesh has released Tk 5 billion (~$40.6 million) to Bangladesh Bank for incentives and financial aid to export-oriented sectors in FY 2026-27. 
The CGA issued debit authority on September 30 under the Finance Division's subsidies and incentives budget. 
The allocation covers textiles, leather goods, seafood and other approved exports, plus 1 per cent aid for RMG exports.

title: Bangladesh seeks end to Indian anti-dumping duties on jute, PET film
summary:
Bangladesh has urged India to remove land port export restrictions and anti-dumping duties on Bangladeshi jute products and PET film at the 16th Joint Working Group on Trade meeting in New Delhi.
Dhaka also sought continued tariff preferences after LDC graduation, improved border infrastructure, faster cargo clearance and stronger regional connectivity to boost bilateral trade.

title: India, ASEAN seek faster progress on trade agreement review
summary:
ASEAN hosted the 15th AITIGA Joint Committee in Jakarta from October 6-9, where India and ASEAN reviewed negotiations on the trade-in-goods pact and directed sub-committees to accelerate pending review chapters.
Three of eight sub-committees met on legal issues, market access and rules of origin.
The next hybrid Joint Committee meeting is due in India in January 2027.

title: India’s ₹10,000-cr SME fund: Can textile exporters tap it?
summary:
India’s ₹10,000-crore (~$1.03 billion) SME Growth Fund could help textile exporters fund capacity, technology and compliance, but it is not confirmed financing.
The AIF has ₹500 crore budgeted for FY2026–27 and is designed for direct equity in mainly manufacturing-focused SMEs.
With no textile allocation, manager or eligibility rules yet, exporters should focus on audited, investment-ready plans.

title: Europe moves to extend anti-VAT fraud tools to June 2030
summary:
European Commission has proposed extending two EU anti-VAT fraud tools to June 2030, beyond their June 30, 2026 expiry, during wider reform. 
The Reverse Charge and Quick Reaction mechanisms target missing trader fraud in fraud-sensitive or newly hit sectors. 
The plan precedes VIDA digital reporting, mandatory e-invoicing and real-time cross-border reporting, and now goes to the Council.

title: Germany’s €9.3 bn footwear market and the rise of sneakers
summary:
Germany’s footwear market is forecast to shrink for a third year in 2026, but TexPro says textile-upper imports rose 0.5 per cent to $3.06 billion in January-July.
HS 640419 footwear with textile uppers and rubber or plastic soles grew 6.3 per cent to $1.94 billion, while specified textile sports shoes fell 8.5 per cent.
China and Vietnam lead supply; EU inventory rules sharpen sourcing.

title: US apparel CPI rises 3.7% year-on-year in August: Cotton Inc
summary:
US apparel CPI rose 0.1 per cent month on month in August after two declines and was 3.7 per cent higher year on year, with recent CPI levels the highest since 1999, Cotton Incorporated said.
Cotton-dominant apparel import costs rose to $3.77 per square metre equivalent, excluding tariffs.
Real apparel spending grew 1.3 per cent month on month and 3.9 per cent year on year.

title: Albania's apparel imports surge 20% while exports remain flat
summary:
Albania's apparel imports rose 19.90 per cent to $278.181 million in January–July 2026, while exports slipped 0.14 per cent to $387.080 million, narrowing the trade surplus by about 30 per cent.
China drove import growth, lifting its share to 23.92 per cent; Italy remained the top supplier.
Exports relied on Italy, Greece and Germany, with Germany down 26.80 per cent.

title: Britain’s unworn clothes waste billions of litres of water: Oxfam
summary:
An Oxfam UK report has claimed that social media is fuelling fast fashion, placing digital influence in focus for the apparel and fashion sector. 
It found that 32 per cent of the average UK wardrobe has not been worn in the past year, while four in 10 people have worn an item of clothing just once. 
The water used to produce those barely worn garments would fill about 88 billion single-use water bottles.

title: Myanmar garment closures: Is responsible exit now a buyer risk?
summary:
Myanmar’s garment closures are turning human-rights due diligence into a commercial and reputational risk for buyers still sourcing from the country.
Teng Hui in Yangon is preparing a temporary suspension after reduced orders, with 2,355 of 2,610 workers seeking transfers.
Japan’s Myanmar imports rose to $1.68 billion in 2025, with clothing and accessories at 78.5 per cent.

title: US' AAFA targets online counterfeits in USTR review submission
summary:

title: Cambodia, Indonesia ship $5.6 bn in US apparel: China losing ground?

TexPro data shows imports fell 8.30 per cent to $44.06 billion, with China and India driving most of the net decline.
Gains came mainly from stronger category positions, but value pressure and textile dependencies remain risks.

title: India’s garment exports fell $575 mn. What went wrong?
summary:
India’s garment exports fell 10.38 per cent to $4.967 billion in April–July 2026, a $575.49-million loss, while yarn-and-thread exports rose 17.15 per cent to $1.846 billion.
The US drove 69 per cent of the net fall, with exports there down 21.41 per cent to $1.466 billion.
Recovery needs stronger volumes, market share, factory utilisation and jobs, not just a less severe contraction.

title: Australia’s apparel imports decline to $1.47 bn in July-Aug 2026
summary:

Fibre imports rose slightly to Au$23 million, but textile fibre exports eased 14.44 per cent to Au$1.155 billion and cotton exports fell 17.70 per cent in August.
ABS data showed mixed trade.

title: Bangladesh's apparel exports to US rebound in August
summary:

China and Vietnam posted modest gains, while Cambodia and India declined in August shipments to the US.
For January-August, Bangladesh shipments were about $5.39 billion, down 4.17 per cent from about $5.62 billion.
